title: A working day — present-tense verbs
goal: Describe your daily routine with the first full set of verb endings: indefinite conjugation, six persons, three vowel groups.
bekal: build the *én*, *te*, *ő*, *mi*, *ti*, *ők* forms of any verb yourself
recognize verbs ending in *s*, *sz*, *z* whose "you" form is different
tell the story of your working day from waking up to going to bed

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Egy hétköznap
dialogs.intro: Anna is curious what it is like to work in Budapest as a foreigner. Budi describes his ordinary day.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.id: What do you do on a weekday?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Reggel hatkor kelek. Aztán zuhanyozom és reggelizem.
lines.id: I get up at six in the morning. Then I shower and have breakfast.
lines.literal: morning six-at I-get-up. then I-shower and I-breakfast.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.id: When do you leave the house?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: At half past seven. I take the metro to work.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Egy irodában, a Blaha Lujza téren. Kilenctől ötig dolgozom.
lines.id: In an office on Blaha Lujza tér. I work from nine to five.
lines.literal: an office-in, the Blaha Lujza square-on. nine-from five-until I-work.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Igen, délben eszem valamit a kollégákkal.
lines.id: Yes, at noon I eat something with my colleagues.
lines.literal: yes, noon-at I-eat something-OBJ the colleague-PL-with.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.id: What do you do in the evening?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Magyarul tanulok, olvasok, néha sportolok. Tizenegy körül alszom.
lines.id: I study Hungarian, I read, sometimes I exercise. Around eleven I go to sleep.
lines.literal: Hungarian-ly I-study, I-read, sometimes I-exercise. eleven around I-sleep.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Az kevés! Én nyolc órát alszom.
lines.id: That's not much! I sleep eight hours.
lines.literal: that little! I eight hour-OBJ I-sleep.

notes: **The pronoun is almost always dropped.** *Kelek* already means "I get up", *dolgozol* already means "you work". The ending carries the person, so *én* and *te* appear only for emphasis — look at the last line: *Én nyolc órát alszom* = "**I** sleep eight hours" (unlike you).

**Nyolc órát alszom** uses the object ending to express **duration**. Hungarian treats duration like an object: *két órát várok* (I wait two hours), *egy hetet maradok* (I stay a week). The habit is not hard; it just needs noticing once.

**Metróval, a kollégákkal.** The "with" ending attaches and assimilates its *v*, as you saw in Unit 7. After a plural, the result is *-kkal / -kkel*: *kollégák* → *kollégákkal*. The full rule is in Unit 15.
**Megyek dolgozni** uses the *-ni* base form to express purpose: "I go to work". Just like English "I go to work" — no extra word for "to" needed.
**Kilenctől ötig** closes a stretch of time with a pair of endings: *-tól/-től* (from) and *-ig* (until). The pair is also used for places: *Budapesttől Szegedig* (from Budapest to Szeged).

**Zuhanyozom, reggelizem, dolgozom, alszom.** All end in *-om/-em* in the "I" form, not *-ok/-ek*. That is the sign of the **-ik group**: verbs whose dictionary form ends in *-ik*. This group is covered in the third box below.

grammars.title: Indefinite conjugation — the first set of endings
body: Six persons, three vowel groups. Notice that the pattern is identical in all three columns; only the linking vowel differs, exactly as with the possessive endings in Unit 5.
after: **The ő row is a gift.** The third person singular is the bare verb itself, with nothing added. That is why Hungarian dictionaries list the *ő* form rather than the infinitive — the shortest form is also the most frequently used.
**The te form has two faces.** *-sz* is used for most verbs, but verbs ending in a hissing sound take *-ol/-el/-öl*. The next table covers them.

**The present also means "am doing" and "will do".** *Tanulok* can mean "I study", "I am studying" and — if the time is clear — "I will study". Hungarian does not distinguish the three, just as English often doesn't for the future ("I leave tomorrow").

grammars.title: Verbs ending in s, sz, z, dz
body: One small adjustment in the "you" form, and that's all.
after: The reason is purely phonetic: *-sz* after *s* or *z* cannot be pronounced clearly. Hungarian chooses a linking vowel rather than forcing the tongue.
The other five forms do not change at all: *olvasok, olvasol, olvas, olvasunk, olvastok, olvasnak*.

grammars.title: The -ik group
body: A set of verbs whose dictionary form ends in *-ik*. Only the first two rows differ.
after: This group contains many everyday verbs: *lakik, dolgozik, alszik, eszik, iszik, utazik, zuhanyozik, reggelizik, ebédel* (this one is not *-ik*, careful), *érkezik, találkozik, kezdődik*.
**In everyday speech, many Hungarians also use *-ok* for this group** — *lakok* instead of *lakom*. It is not considered a serious mistake, but the *-om* form is always correct, so use that.

blocks.text: Notice *felkel*: it is *kel* with the prefix *fel-* (up). Prefixes like this change and sharpen the meaning of a verb, and they are one of the most distinctive features of Hungarian. Unit 12 covers them.
These two little groups of words turn a list of activities into a story.
*Soha* always goes with *nem*: *Soha nem főzök* = "I never cook". Hungarian uses **double negation** and considers it correct — like Spanish or Italian, and unlike standard English.

blocks.title: The most productive speaking practice at this level
items: Tell your own day out loud, from waking up to going to bed, using only ten verbs. Do it every day for a week.

Then tell your **friend's** day — the same sentences, but with every verb in the *ő* form. This is the hidden exercise that fastest installs the whole table in your head, because you change the form while thinking about the content, not while staring at a table.

exercises.prompt: Write the én, te and ő forms of these verbs.
Fill in the blanks with the right verb form.

items: I get up at six in the morning.
I work from nine to five.
What do you do in the evening?
